binding_declaration_evidence: data sccache_stats_query_does_not_spawn_note: String = "MEASURED CORRECTION, 2026-08-01: `--show-stats` does NOT auto-start a server, and the widely-repeated claim that 'any sccache invocation auto-starts a server, so --show-stats manufactures the evidence it reports' is FALSE for sccache 0.15.0. Two controls on srv2, each with a PRIVATE cache dir AND a private endpoint so the falsifier could not touch production: with SCCACHE_SERVER_UDS the socket did not exist before or after the call; with a private SCCACHE_SERVER_PORT the listener count was 0 before and 0 after. In both the call returned rc=0 and printed a fully-formed table of ZEROES. A third control isolated what DOES spawn: one real compile (`sccache /usr/bin/gcc -c t.c`) through the same private port took the listener count 0 -> 1, and the new server inherited the INVOKING process's cgroup (observed: the caller's own session scope). THE DEFECT IS REAL BUT DIFFERENTLY SHAPED, and the difference changes the remedy's justification rather than the remedy: --show-stats answers plausibly WITHOUT a server existing at all, so a read-back that converges on it greens over a host with no durable daemon — a fabricated plausible output (DESIGN section 5), which is exactly what srv3 exhibited on 2026-07-25 (a full stats table while the unit had been inactive six hours). The observation there was right; the inference drawn from it — that the call had created a server — was wrong. Consequence for the observer: stats is supplemental data gathered AFTER ownership is independently established, never the thing that establishes it; and the auto-spawn wall belongs on the COMPILE path, which is where a client actually creates a server in its own cgroup."

Currently, this option chooses a bucket location in the closest available region to the create bucket request based on the location of the caller. Location Hints are optional parameters you can provide during bucket creation to indicate the primary geographical location you expect data will be accessed from. Location Hints are a best effort and not a guarantee, and they should only be used as a way to optimize performance. Available hints: wnam Western North America, enam Eastern North America, weur Western Europe, eeur Eastern Europe, apac Asia-Pacific, oc Oceania. Jurisdictional Restrictions guarantee objects in a bucket are stored within a specific jurisdiction. Use Jurisdictional Restrictions when you need to ensure data is stored and processed within a jurisdiction to meet data residency requirements. Available jurisdictions: eu European Union, fedramp FedRAMP, us United States. The following services do not interact with R2 resources with assigned jurisdictions: Logpush. Once an R2 bucket is created, the jurisdiction cannot be changed. Page last updated Aug 19, 2026. Read 2026-09-12."

data r2_how_r2_works_reading: NonEmptyStr = "R2 Gateway: The entry point for all API requests that handles authentication and routing logic. This service is deployed across Cloudflare's global network via Cloudflare Workers. Metadata Service: A distributed layer built on Durable Objects used to store and manage object metadata. Distributed Storage Infrastructure: The underlying infrastructure that persistently stores encrypted object data. On write, the Gateway determines which storage cluster to write the encrypted data to within the location set for the bucket. The encrypted data is written and stored in the distributed storage infrastructure, and replicated within the region (e.g. ENAM) for durability. On read, if the object is not in the tiered read cache, it retrieves the object from one of the distributed storage data centers within the region that holds the object data. Page last updated Apr 21, 2026. Read 2026-09-12."

data r2_us_jurisdiction_changelog_reading: NonEmptyStr = "New us jurisdiction for R2. Use the jurisdiction-specific S3 endpoint https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.us.r2.cloudflarestorage.com. Once an R2 bucket is created, its jurisdiction cannot be changed. Posted 2026-08-17. Read 2026-09-12."

data spark_verify_wrapper_local_wet_enrolment_note: String = "A NOTE STOOD HERE CLAIMING THE WET VERIFY CONTRACT WAS UNWRITABLE, AND IT WAS FALSE. It read three constructors -- TransportScript, cli_surface_of_literal_words and ArgvCommand -- concluded that every route from rendered text to a running process is closed to a witness, and justified DELETING the file that tried. Two of those three readings were correct about their own wall. The conclusion drawn from them was not.

THE ADMITTED ROUTE EXISTS AND WAS SIMPLY NOT FOUND. extdeps.posix.sh_invocation.posix_sh_program_command appears in argv_command's own admit_callers list, and gunbc.command_runner.run_shell_command_observe appears in cli_surface_of_literal_words'. Composing those two is a witness driving PRODUCTION BUILDERS, which is precisely what the walls require: they forbid MINTING an argv, never running one that an admitted builder produced. The deleted file's actual defect was that it minted its own; the remedy was composition, not abandonment.

AND THE SUBJECT IS THE BUILDER'S INTENDED CASE. posix_sh_program_command's annotation refuses a caller spelling one program's argv inside a string; what this contract tests is a genuine shell PROGRAM BODY -- `cmd; rc=$?; if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then echo OK; else echo FAILED; fi; exit $rc`. The previous deletion was argued from the wall's purpose, and the purpose points the other way.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE FILE: the false note recorded an IMPOSSIBILITY on a carrier. A wrong value is caught the first time it is used; a wrong impossibility is never used at all, and every later reader inherits it as settled. It sat beside a correct observation -- that bin_witness_wet_entries has had no executing consumer since 2026-08-15 -- which made the whole row read as established.

CURRENT STANDING: the contract is locally executable through an admitted production bridge and is enrolled in the LocalRepoWetLane schedule, whose cadence executes and produces candidate-bound terminals. What was missing was enrolment and composition, never substrate capability."

data known_red_frontier_note: String = "HOW THE KNOWN-RED FRONTIER WORKS, and the receipts it has accumulated. The rows themselves live at function grain on gunbc.explicit_witness_admission explicit_witness_admissions, each carrying its own diagnosis and dissolve_on; this note deliberately does NOT restate them (that would be the parallel-ledger duplication the rows exist to prevent) and carries only what is not a property of a live row. WHAT THEY ARE: witnesses red on main for feature gaps owned by named lanes. They are RED CONTROLS for their lanes, not broken tests - deleting one would discard the discriminating input, while leaving it discovered would red every wide PR on a debt that PR did not create. So each sits as a declared, countable row (the typed self-host-frontier pattern applied to witnesses). Local recipe per row: claim_batch --source-root dag --source-root src/v2 --entry <entry> --functions <function> -- AND FOR AN ExecutionWitnessKind ROW, --wet AS WELL, WITHOUT WHICH THE RECIPE CANNOT DO WHAT THE ROW ASKS OF IT. claim_batch is hermetic by default, so a wet row invoked by the recipe as written above never reaches its subject: measured 2026-08-26 on self_host_logic_behavioral_receipt_holds, it returns FAIL in 87 seconds with 'hermetic route has no arm for Dir: the claim never reached its subject, so this is a route gap and not a verdict', naming three undeclared dispatches (Filesystem.Read, git.Inspect.Toplevel, shell.Mktemp.Dir). The refusal is well-modeled and says plainly that it is not a verdict; the defect was in the recipe, which every wet dissolution condition below cites as the way its row greens. A row whose only recorded closing move cannot close it is the shape DESIGN records for a gate whose sole green is the forbidden action -- here arrived at from the other side, with no green reachable at all. THE ROSTER MUST NOT GROW SILENTLY: a new admission requires a per-row reason naming the diagnosis and owner plus a dissolve_on, and a row whose witness runs green locally is stale and deletes. Greening is the counted un-quarantine event of std.witness_admission: the row deletes in the SAME change that lands the fix, which promotes the unchanged witness to ordinary DiscoverySelection as a permanent regression control (DESIGN 4b(4) - the climb deletes the quarantine machinery, never the evidence). UN-QUARANTINE RECEIPTS (history, not live rows). emit_host_fold_closure_equals_eval_test (2026-07-20, smart-hawk-154 / witness-realization lane 3): three rows deleted - the eval walk now materializes RuntimeClosure for an Arrow TypeNode in runtime-argument position (eval_fold_is_closure_argument_edge / eval_fold_closure_argument_child_state in 05_eval.dag), so the closure at transform child 3 of fold_fixture_param_call_body evaluates to a real closure value instead of falling through eval_type_node_atom's non-Atom arm into allocate_literal and refusing. The interpreted leg reads the closure from the EVALUATED argument list rather than re-walking the node AST, so eval is genuinely exercised, and no literal-atom roster was extended (the PR 6879 diagnosis-table tripwire). emit_on_demand_field_access_family_witness_test + emit_on_demand_complement_family_witness_test (2026-07-20, witty-owl-841 / eval-repair arc): ten rows deleted - dag_node_is_eval_literal_atom plus eval_type_node_atom bind-miss and non-Atom TypeNode arms routing to allocate_literal repaired the lane-2 equals_eval BuildFailed roots. emit_host_meet_join_equals_eval_test and emit_host_variant_construct_equals_eval_test greened as byproducts of the same consolidation and never held rows of their own. WET ASSEMBLE-RED SelfEmitted MODULE RECEIPTS (admitted 2026-07-25, review #7199) are the same frontier at a different WitnessKind: six SelfEmitted wet behavioral receipts red on assemble (unresolved std_algebra/std_types/std_nat/List and target_carriers type-shape, cadence run 30126573464), which run Wet expect_red on the falsifier quarantine batch because Phase-0 forbids SelfEmitted-with-zero-executing-consumer. As of 2026-08-03 they are ExecutionWitnessKind rows on the one admission authority beside the hermetic ones, and v2.compiler.self_host.seed_emitter_behavioral_wet_known_red_entries derives from it rather than holding its own copy. Owner: #7199 falsifier lane / self-host assemble."

data v1_claim_scoped_witness_batch_deleted_note: String = "THE SCOPED WITNESS BATCH IS DELETED (2026-08-15), and with it the only ScopedWitnessBatch instance that ever existed. It ran five file-grain v1 claim entries under a dag plus src/v1 source-root envelope, in a sequential child worker, so the v1 compiler closure could be resolved without widening witness_layer_roots for everything else.

WHY IT COULD NOT SURVIVE AFFECTED-SET SELECTION. It was the last SelectionApplied consumer on the required path, and its 720-second clamp was derived (PR #8259) from a measured 565-second wall on the assumption that unrelated PRs skip it. With selection deleted the two available readings were both wrong: run it every PR and the required floor grows by roughly nine minutes under a clamp basis that no longer describes it, or keep a selection mechanism alive for one batch. Its cost was also never really the witnesses — the same receipt measured about 390 seconds of closure materialization before the first witness line and about 30 seconds of witness evaluation, so it was paying a whole second subject preparation to check thirty rows.

WHAT THIS NARROWS, stated rather than implied: the entries under src/v1/tests/claim have NO executing consumer. They are not covered by ordinary discovery, whose roots are dag plus src/v2. Their generated stage0 emissions still compile into the seed crate, which is not execution. This is a real loss of coverage over v1 parser and namespace-binding behavior, taken deliberately as part of deleting the floor rather than discovered later, and it is NOT backstopped by any cadence — the cadence lane those rows might have moved to was refused for the same reason the per-PR slot was: a second subject envelope is the defect, not the schedule it runs on.

RESTORATION: one prepared subject spanning dag, src/v1 and src/v2, at which point a separate envelope, a separate worker, a separate clamp and a separate receipt family all stop existing and these rows are ordinary discovery."

WHY CAPTURE NEVER ARMED (both halves independently fatal): claim_executor returns from run_required_floor before the --plan-entry branch; capture_begin lives only under plan_function == gunbc_falsifier_plan inside that branch; witnesses.yml invokes only --required-floor; and src/v2/workflow/ci_floor_plan.dag (gunbc_falsifier_plan entry) was deleted by the floor cut — so the global stayed None and every run paid the full resolve cost before the foregone parent plan telemetry was not captured refusal. ENROLLMENT HID THE DEFECT: expected-red held means merely not-Pass, so a row failing structurally was indistinguishable from a row failing for the reason it was enrolled for — hiding 43% of slow time for the entire life of the floor, not a small miss. Measured: 526.1s wall, 4.6x next module, +2.66GB RSS. DELETED end-to-end: witness, transport, resolution_divergence_census bin, walk_target_alias_plan bin and cli_run walk-target planner (same silent-pick investigation family; zero CI consumers), in-process builtin, cli_run census machinery, falsifier roster rows. REBUILD CONSTRAINT: do NOT substitute the calling witness InterpContext for a whole-corpus census subject — the floor evaluates each claim through claim_scope_for, which scopes to that module's transitive import closure, not the prepared subject; reusing _calling_ctx (the obvious cheap repair) would silently narrow coverage from the whole corpus to one witness closure, run fast, report plausible sites_checked, and cover almost nothing (empty-observation narrow: bottom-as-answer conflated with bottom-as-ignorance). A future census must take the prepared module list explicitly; terminal shape is a function over that list whose typed receipt a constant-time witness asserts — not a witness that acquires or inherits its subject at evaluation time."

data gunbc_ci_floor_batch_wall_budget_note: String = "SUPERSEDED by the derived clamp gunbc_ci_floor_batch_clamp_note (Piece 3, 2026-07-24): the hand-set gunbc_ci_floor_batch_wall_budget_seconds list this note governed is deleted, replaced by overhead + units*rate computed at run time; this note is kept for the operator-signed static-era history (including the two 1320->1440->1680 raises below) and the raise discipline, which carries forward to the clamp constants. THE COST WALL (CI floor endgame D5, operator brief 2026-07-23 — the resolve-regression journey's section-3 finding made mechanism: nothing redded a merge that added floor minutes, so every recovered minute was re-spent by the next lane's enrollment, and the step timeout's own bounce history 30 -> 60 -> 90 -> 120 -> 180 -> 270 -> 55 is the record of the budget being raised to fit). Per-BATCH wall budgets for gunbc_ci_floor_plan (named gunbc_ci_floor_batches through the static era this note records), enforced by claim_executor at walk time: each batch's measured wall is recorded as a typed receipt row (target/floor-batch-wall-receipt.txt), and a batch over its budget is a typed, located refusal — FLOOR-BATCH-OVER-BUDGET naming the batch index, measured wall, budget row, and this carrier — that reds the walk. A failure arm refuses, never widens: over-budget never triggers a rerun, a wider scope, or a silent cap raise. Denominated PER-BATCH, never per-run, because plumbing PRs have a structurally different cost profile (attribution doc section 9.2: a PR touching host_prelude/cli_run legitimately runs 46 of 55 wet rows — a per-run wall would red every such PR spuriously; per-batch budgets absorb the profile where it lands). RULING RECONCILIATION (the operator dispatching the 2026-07-23 endgame brief is the sign-off on this reading): the standing rule 'no wall-clock term in any verdict' (ci_floor_materialization_receipt_note, operator ruling 2026-07-10) governs WITNESS VERDICTS — a witness's pass/fail must never depend on how long it took. Batch budgets do not touch witness verdicts: they are admission/scheduling facts at the walk grain, the same split the 5-second fast-lane eval law already uses (gunbc_ci_fast_lane_rule_note: the deadline is lane admission, not a verdict term), so a batch refusal names the BATCH, and every witness verdict inside it stands as evaluated. RAISE DISCIPLINE: raising any budget requires appending a dated receipt note here naming the run id and the enrollment that grew the batch — the same discipline as the timeout-note bounce history — never a silent number edit. Budget basis (run 30009199696, post-#7122, with the endgame fixes priced in): batch 1 cheap gates 185s measured -> 125s post-pool, budget 240; batch 2 receipt consume ~0s, budget 60; batch 3 discovery 1024s measured (corpus-denominated resolve wall, lever-1 re-diagnosis pending), budget 1320; batch 4 wet corpora 649s plumbing-profile measured -> ~175s post-re-home, budget 420; batch 5 emit-host 7s, budget 120; batch 6 ingest 414s measured (4 composed overlay children — the genuine mktemp constraint), budget 600; batch 7 reads-real-bytes 206s, budget 420. Sum 3180s = 53min under the 55min step cap. OPERATOR SIGNATURE (briansrls, 2026-07-23): the admission/verdict reading above is affirmed — per-batch wall budgets are scheduling-admission facts, not wall-clock terms in witness verdicts; this line is the declared human-signed exemption row the 2026-07-10 ruling requires. Raise discipline amended: RAISING any budget row requires a new dated operator-signed line here naming the run id and the enrollment that grew the batch; TIGHTENING may land by ordinary receipt note. The on-call remedy for FLOOR-BATCH-OVER-BUDGET is diagnose-or-signed-raise, never rerun. FOLLOW-UP ROWS (operator rework push, 2026-07-23): (a) PRELUDE COVERAGE HOLE — the ~5min before batch-1 arms (naming-hygiene walk, policy install, plan resolve/eval, governor arm, eager compile-clean install) sits OUTSIDE every batch budget and can only red at the 55min step cap; a prelude budget row lands when the phase_mark walls get their own receipt keys. (b) IDENTITY-KEYED BUDGETS — rows are keyed by batch INDEX today (the coverage witness pins length, so a schedule change reds loudly rather than misassigning); keying by batch content-identity dissolves the index coupling and rides the ComputationIdentity lane. (c) K-CAP UNION-RSS RECEIPT — cheap_gate_pool_max_claims_per_child=16 is provisional until the pooled child's union RSS is receipted (claim_batch already prints per-shard-peak-rss; the first CI runs' logs back or re-size the cap; local proxy receipt: the 4-gate outer child peaked 1.82GB with the 12-claim pool nested). OPERATOR-SIGNED RAISE (briansrls, 2026-07-24): batch 3 (row index [2]) 1320 -> 1440 seconds, +9.1 percent (operator: 'lets raise the budget slightly more to give it some room over main' / 'like 10%'; 24min keeps the row's whole-minute grain). RUN IDS: 30063268739 @ e7a9006f wall_ms=1629287, 30058048605 wall_ms=1344115, 30055079462 wall_ms=1380561 — all batch=3 against budget_ms=1320000 on PR #7137. THE ENROLLMENT THAT GREW THE BATCH: none, and that mismatch with this discipline's template IS the receipt. Batch 3 is the affected-set-selected discovery corpus, so its wall is denominated in the DIFF's affected entry count, not in a roster edit: #7137 touches gunbc.ci.ci_layer_roots (broadly imported) and src/v1/stage0/src/cli_run.rs, selecting 839-841 entries where a typical main push selects 600-601. The retired 1320 divided by 841 entries = 1.570 s-per-entry, BELOW main's own 1.574 measured rate: the row had zero headroom for any broad-touch diff and would red a no-op PR that merely touched a widely-imported carrier. 1440/841 = 1.712 s-per-entry, ~8.8 percent over main's rate — that is the 'room over main'. Ceilings are per-batch maxima rather than a predicted run wall, but the sum was this note's stated safety argument and it no longer holds with margin, so it is recorded here rather than dropped. FOLLOW-UP (not landed here): restore margin by TIGHTENING the rows with the largest declared-vs-measured gap once post-merge receipts exist — batch 4 (budget 420, ~175s measured post-re-home) and batch 6 (budget 600, 414s measured) — which lands by ordinary receipt note under this same discipline. OPERATOR-SIGNED RAISE (briansrls, 2026-07-24, second): batch 3 (row index [2]) 1440 -> 1680 seconds, +16.7 percent (28min, whole-minute grain). Operator's word this raise: 'you may bump the budget to 1680 - we're redoing it completely anyway' — so 1680 is a STOPGAP to green this PR while the batch-budget mechanism itself is reworked (the FOLLOW-UP ROWS above: prelude coverage, identity-keyed budgets, k-cap union-RSS), not a claim that 1680 is the settled ceiling. data gunbc_ci_compile_clean_clamp_note: String = "COMPILE-CLEAN LEG CLAMP (prelude coverage, first slice): discharges the compile-clean portion of gunbc_ci_floor_batch_clamp_note FOLLOW-UP ROW (a) — the eager compile-clean install ran OUTSIDE every batch budget and could only red at the step cap, which is how a 15m32s green gate grew past 49 minutes across #7398/#7438 with nothing naming the growth (typecheck-perf investigation, PR #7490). Same shape as the batch clamps: clamp_ms = overhead_seconds*1000 + closure_units * per_unit_ms, where closure_units is the compiled closure's MODULE COUNT — a runtime fact of the scope disposition (whole-tree ~2725 today, affected-set proportional to the diff), so the clamp re-denominates with scope exactly as batch clamps re-denominate with the affected set. Over-clamp is FLOOR-COMPILE-CLEAN-OVER-BUDGET: a typed, located walk refusal (admission grain — the compile receipt's ok is untouched, per the signed admission/verdict split in gunbc_ci_floor_batch_wall_budget_note); never a rerun, never a widen. RED-control hook GUNBC_FLOOR_COMPILE_CLEAN_BUDGET_TIGHTEN_MS lowers the computed clamp (min), never raises. GROWTH DETECTION at row grain is NOT this clamp's job (the family margin ruling, 2026-07-25): per-row 2x drift against dated basis rows rides gunbc.witness.witness_row_cost's comparator over dag/gunbc/compile_clean_cost_basis.tsv — the pass + module_typecheck rows of target/floor-compile-clean-cost-receipt.tsv, basis rows citing arm64 fleet run ids only, BasisAbsent counted until seeded from a cited run's own receipt FILE (the #7475 seeding pattern; an empty basis must count loudly, never read as no-drift). SEEDING SOURCE CORRECTED: this clause used to name the [compile-clean-cost] log lines, because the receipt file had no way off the runner and every row was mirrored into the step log to compensate — ~1,690 lines per floor run, and the same shape cost 8,614 more on the disclosure receipt. THAT REPLACEMENT ROUTE IS NOW GONE TOO, which is the correction this clause carries: it used to say the ci job uploads the receipts as the floor-receipts artifact via gunbc.ci_workflow ci_floor_receipts_upload_step, so seeding downloads the TSV instead of scraping a log. No live workflow carries that step -- it died with ci.yml in the floor cut. TRANSPORT IS NOW PARTIAL RATHER THAN ABSENT, and this clause is written at that grain because the coarser claim went stale within a day: gunbc#8875 (2026-08-22) added an upload to witnesses.yml, so DISPOSITION receipts DO leave the runner today. gunbc#8877 then replaced that single bundled artifact with one artifact per file -- required-floor-disposition, expected-red-roster-join and long-home-storage-agreement -- because the bundled form evaluates if-no-files-found once over the combined list and so cannot report a single missing file. A reader looking for the name required-floor-receipts will not find it; the population is unchanged and none of the cost receipts this note names are in any of the three. So the gap is no longer the absence of any transport; it is that the transport which exists carries a different population, and a reader who sees an artifact on a green run must not infer that these receipts are in it. So this note deliberately retired the log route in favour of an artifact route that was then deleted underneath it, and both of its named routes are inoperative. THE PRODUCER IS UNREACHABLE ON THE NAMED INVOCATION AS WELL, so restoring transport alone would not seed anything: install_floor_compile_clean_receipt's claim_executor caller sits below the required_floor_mode early return, and the only path that could reach it under required CI is the install_or_consume_floor_compile_clean_gate_receipt builtin, whose live .dag caller sits in dag/gunbc/instruments/dag_compile_clean_transport -- reached by compile-clean witnesses that are themselves ROUTE-GAPPED and never arrive at their subject. Measured on the certified main run: zero compile-clean-cost markers. NO BASIS MAY BE INFERRED FROM THE AGGREGATE LOG OR FABRICATED FROM AN ABSENT RECEIPT -- an empty basis must count loudly, exactly as this note already requires of BasisAbsent, and that requirement is what forbids papering over the gap while it stands, and the writers no longer mirror their bodies. The log lines are GONE, not merely deprecated: a seeding attempt that greps a run log for them will find nothing, which is why this clause is corrected rather than left to rot. BASIS OF THE CONSTANTS (worker-sized, 2026-07-31, from run 30602520347 @ 0ecb898, host srv1-01 arm64, post-#7490 fixes): whole-tree pass 258s over the ~1648-unit whole-tree entry closure (units = the leg's compiled closure module count, receipted by the first [compile-clean-cost] execution — NOT the ~2725-file module index, which overcounts by pool files outside every entry closure) = ~157ms/unit observed; per_unit_ms 320 is ~2x that rate, funding a full 2x fleet-spread host on top of the observed wall (the family margin ruling: a breach means content grew, never which host answered; pre-fix completing runs spread ~1.8x across hosts) — the batch family's 1000ms coefficient carries 1.4-1.7x the same way; overhead 60s covers the closure-size-independent tail (census fill parse ~13s fleet + governor arm). Whole-tree clamp = 60s + 1648*320ms = ~587s (~2.3x the observed 258s fleet wall). MECHANISM RECEIPTS (local x86, logic-not-cost host): green e2e via gunbc_ci_plan_artifact_plan — pass 310127ms/1648 units, WithinBudget, 1204 module rows, drift basis_absent=1205 counted, exit 0 (run at the pre-resize 200ms sizing; the arm proof is arithmetic-independent and the formula is witness-pinned at the final constants); RED control via GUNBC_FLOOR_COMPILE_CLEAN_BUDGET_TIGHTEN_MS=1 receipted beside it. DISPATCH: operator direction this session ('can we add the budget gating ... i suggest we share that model' — briansrls, 2026-07-31). data gunbc_ci_compile_clean_clamp_note: String = "COMPILE-CLEAN LEG CLAMP (prelude coverage, first slice): discharges the compile-clean portion of gunbc_ci_floor_batch_clamp_note FOLLOW-UP ROW (a) — the eager compile-clean install ran OUTSIDE every batch budget and could only red at the step cap, which is how a 15m32s green gate grew past 49 minutes across #7398/#7438 with nothing naming the growth (typecheck-perf investigation, PR #7490). Over-clamp is FLOOR-COMPILE-CLEAN-OVER-BUDGET: a typed, located walk refusal (admission grain — the compile receipt's ok is untouched, per the signed admission/verdict split in gunbc_ci_floor_batch_wall_budget_note); never a rerun, never a widen. GROWTH DETECTION at row grain is NOT this clamp's job (the family margin ruling, 2026-07-25): per-row 2x drift against dated basis rows rides gunbc.witness.witness_row_cost's comparator over dag/gunbc/compile_clean_cost_basis.tsv — the pass + module_typecheck rows of target/floor-compile-clean-cost-receipt.tsv, basis rows citing arm64 fleet run ids only, BasisAbsent counted until seeded from a cited run's own receipt FILE (the #7475 seeding pattern; an empty basis must count loudly, never read as no-drift). THAT REPLACEMENT ROUTE IS NOW GONE TOO, which is the correction this clause carries: it used to say the ci job uploads the receipts as the floor-receipts artifact via gunbc.ci_workflow ci_floor_receipts_upload_step, so seeding downloads the TSV instead of scraping a log. No live workflow carries that step -- it died with ci.yml in the floor cut. data class_b_accidental_coverage_exception_note: String = "THE ONE NAMED ACCIDENTAL-COVERAGE EXCEPTION for the Class B declared-import-closure observation (operator ruling 2026-08-09). src/v2/std/grounding.dag carries ZERO imports and reaches v2.std.host_run.EmitHostRunReceipt (twice) and v2.std.verdict.VerdictTally by dotted path, so those bind only when some unrelated importer has already pulled those modules into the assembled closure — a live Class B pool-membership-coincidence specimen, the class the import-strip witness-discovery cascade names as the blocker on further dag/** stripping.

TWO ALTERNATIVES WERE REJECTED, and recording why is the point of this row. Widening class_b_declared_import_pool_roots would promote pool-coincidence to gate policy and blind the gate to precisely the class it exists to observe. Restoring grounding.dag's import closure would UN-STRIP an already-stripped module — motion against the namespace lane whose terminal state is deleting the import grammar outright, paid now and unwound later. The third option is the only one leaving both the gate's meaning and the lane's direction intact: the file becomes a COUNTED member of the accidental-coverage population instead of an invisible one, which is strictly more honest than the prior state where it sat in the same condition with nobody counting it.

IT IS A ROSTER OF EXACT (file, type) PAIRS AND NEVER A PATTERN, so it cannot weaken the observation for any other file. Proven by execution rather than asserted: planting a FOURTH unresolved type in that same file returns the gate to false while the three named rows stay exempt, and every exemption is counted and printed at the seam rather than silently dropped — an exemption leaving no trace would be indistinguishable from a clean compile. The realization roster lives at v1_compiler.cli_run CLASS_B_ACCIDENTAL_COVERAGE_EXCEPTIONS, where the diagnostics exist; this row is the authority for WHY it exists and when it dies.

WHAT THE POPULATION IS ACTUALLY REACHED BY, corrected 2026-08-09 (proud-ferret evidence, folded in on operator consolidation). The cascade diagnosis frames this class as a blocker on IMPORT-STRIPPING, which reads as though only a deliberate strip can surface it. It does not: ORDINARY AFFECTED-SET SELECTION reaches it too, because selection narrows the assembled pool, and a bare reference that binds under a wide pool stops binding under a narrow one. That makes the class reachable by any change that shifts which modules a run assembles — a routine PR, not just a strip wave — and it is why the live specimens showed up as CI reds on unrelated lanes rather than during stripping work. The consequence for this roster: its size is NOT a measure of how much stripping has happened, and a quiet corpus is not evidence the population is small. Only a closure-independent binding fix or the provable-coverage check makes the count meaningful.

🟡 dissolve-on: the closure-independent binding fix, or the provable-coverage construction check, that the import-strip cascade names as the unblock condition for dag/** stripping. When either lands, grounding.dag binds from its own declared closure and the roster goes to zero rows."

effect_sites.source: "EVIDENCE, EXECUTED, 2026-09-19 on srv1 (a shared 502 GiB host carrying six live CI runner slots and 400+ sessions). A probe intended to verify that a cgroup memory receipt survives an OOM kill placed its child with `echo $PID > $CG/cgroup.procs` inside a block carrying `2>/dev/null`. The write failed EPERM -- a pid cannot be moved ACROSS a delegation boundary, from `session-N.scope` into a cgroup under `user@1000.service` -- so the 256 MiB cap was never applied and an unbounded allocation loop ran free. The shape was repeated once before it was noticed. The host went from roughly 315 GiB available to 29 GiB. Measured aftermath: no collateral damage -- the only OOM kill in the window was a correctly-capped earlier probe with `constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG`, and all six runner slots stayed loaded/active/running -- but the absence of harm was luck, not construction.",

So Verify has a target that can genuinely go red, the red is the ticket's own acceptance condition rather than a planted fixture, and the transition red -> green IS the work being finished. Together the two bindings pin both directions: one proves the path executes, the other proves it discriminates, and neither claim is available from the other.

The witness is enrolled QuarantineProbeExpectRed in gunbc.ci.ci_layer_roots so a deliberately-red acceptance test does not red the corpus — the cadence built for precisely this, where greening is a counted un-quarantine event and not a silent pass."

process_entry_root_evidence: data belt_actuate_workdir_note: String = "Two DISTINCT workdirs, because the belt's two host verbs bind to different roots (a §5 fail-open otherwise: observing from a repo path that may not exist on an arbitrary host would make `tmux ls` fail and — before this split — get widened to an empty session set). belt_actuate_workdir is the SPAWN root: `git worktree add` must run inside the gunbc repo — a PROJECTION of gunbc.host.host_layout.srv1_gunbc_repo_root (the single path authority; its former private copy deleted, DESIGN §3): the same tree `gunbc serve` loads, which is why dispatch works in-process. belt_observe_workdir is the host-global root '/': `tmux ls` and `tmux kill-session` act on the per-user tmux server (a host singleton, not a repo), so they must run from a directory guaranteed to exist on the host — never the repo path, which may be absent (fake-claude test box, a freshly-enrolled srvN). Observe/teardown therefore carry no workdir parameter; only spawn is workdir-parameterized."

data belt_publish_pass_note: String = "PUBLICATION IS THE ATTEMPT'S LAST OBLIGATION, run by the attempt's own unit once its head is reviewed (gunbc.roadmap.roadmap_belt_obligation PublishObligation; dogfood intervention #6 moved it off the tick). It is still a desired obligation reconciled against an observed one, and a producer nobody calls is still the defect this lane keeps producing, so the wiring is the deliverable, not the type.\\n\\nIT IS AN OBSERVATION OF THE REMOTE AS WELL AS AN EFFECT: running it records the true state - the branch is not published yet - and its next run revises it. The gate is what makes repetition safe, since only a receipt saying the head is on offer stops the revisions, and one PR per work item is ensured, never created twice.\\n\\nTHE TICK HOLDS NO CREDENTIAL AT ALL, and that is what this pass gave up in exchange for the publication boundary. It used to probe GITHUB_TOKEN once per tick and hand the source to every attempt; it now writes a typed request per attempt and reads the answer the publication helper wrote under its own principal. The cost is that a head is published on the SECOND run of its obligation rather than the first: the first writes the request, and the helper's answer arriving is the event that runs it again (the deployment's publication-answer path unit). The gain is that no process holding this token spawns a provider session. See gunbc.roadmap.roadmap_publication_helper for the boundary argument."

data belt_publish_pass_note: String = "PUBLICATION IS THE ATTEMPT'S LAST OBLIGATION, run by the attempt's own unit once its head is reviewed (gunbc.roadmap.roadmap_belt_obligation PublishObligation; dogfood intervention #6 moved it off the tick). It is still a desired obligation reconciled against an observed one, and a producer nobody calls is still the defect this lane keeps producing, so the wiring is the deliverable, not the type.\\n\\nIT IS AN OBSERVATION OF THE REMOTE AS WELL AS AN EFFECT: running it records the true state - the branch is not published yet - and its next run revises it. The gate is what makes repetition safe, since only a receipt saying the head is on offer stops the revisions, and one PR per work item is ensured, never created twice.\\n\\nTHE TICK HOLDS NO CREDENTIAL AT ALL, and that is what this pass gave up in exchange for the publication boundary. It used to probe GITHUB_TOKEN once per tick and hand the source to every attempt; it now writes a typed request per attempt and reads the answer the publication helper wrote under its own principal. The cost is that a head is published on the SECOND run of its obligation rather than the first: the first writes the request, and the helper's answer arriving is the event that runs it again (the deployment's publication-answer path unit). The gain is that no process holding this token spawns a provider session. See gunbc.roadmap.roadmap_publication_helper for the boundary argument."

# Serves HTTPS with a certificate made on first start; the dashboard pins it on first contact.
# Logs: /root/serve/events.log (steps) and /root/serve/serve.log (server, including the download)
D=/root/serve; mkdir -p $D /cache/kv; ev()\{ echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*" >> $D/events.log; }
# Template env is on PID 1; an on-start shell may not inherit it.
for v in POOL_API_KEY PORT CACHE_MODE; do
  [ -n "$\{!v}" ] || export $v="$(tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/1/environ | sed -n "s/^$v=//p")"
done
for v in POOL_API_KEY PORT; do [ -n "$\{!v}" ] || \{ ev "REFUSED: $v not set in template env"; exit 1; }; done
DRV=$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader | head -1)
[ "$\{DRV%%.*}" -ge 580 ] || \{ ev "REFUSED: driver $DRV;

process_entry_root_evidence: data real_execution_home_doc: String = "Wet execution witness for the merge=generated-artifact driver. It builds a real throwaway git repository, binds merge.generated-artifact.driver to a real driver value, drives a real three-way merge, and reads the real index and worktree back — shell.Mktemp.Dir, Filesystem.Write/Read, shell.Remove.RecursiveForce, and the git.Core integration operations have no mock_response, so this file is excluded from hermetic discovery (gunbc.ci.ci_layer_roots witness_exclusion_frontier) and re-enrolled in bin_witness_wet_entries. THE DRIVER TEXT IS NOT COPIED: the temp repository's script is written from expected_generated_artifact_merge_driver_sh, the same emitter the committed .githooks artifact projects, and its config value from the same generated_artifact_merge_driver_config_value_at shaping, so a change to the emitted script is a change to what this witness executes. THE PAIR IS THE POINT. divergent_generated_artifact_merge_refuses is the positive claim. divergent_generated_artifact_merge_under_true_driver_silently_drops_theirs_red_control is the discriminating RED: it is the SAME reproduction with the retired driver value `true`, and it asserts the defect — merge exit 0, no unmerged stage, theirs' content gone — so it fails the moment someone restores take-ours, and it is the executed evidence that the refusal, not the setup, is what makes the divergence loud. one_sided_generated_artifact_change_merges_clean is the non-widen control: with the refusing driver bound, a merge that changed the artifact on one side only must still merge clean and carry the changed content, because git reaches a low-level driver only when both sides moved."

process_entry_root_evidence: data witness_script_producers_note: String = "THE COMMITTED SCRIPT ARTIFACTS ARE GONE, SO THESE WITNESSES CALL THE EMITTER DIRECTLY. Nothing executed .github/live-deploy-srv1-apply.sh or -retract.sh — the real deploy runs live_deploy_apply_prod_role_wet through gunbc run — and their registry rows named a HostReconciler consumer that does not exist. A committed artifact nobody reads is not coverage; it is a false architectural claim that happened to be convenient as a byte oracle.\\n\\nThe coverage did not need the artifact. A fixture sha is forbidden in a committed PRODUCTION artifact, never in a witness, so these call live_deploy_apply_script_for with RevisionBoundAtEmission at the fixture revision and assert the same bytes the golden used to pin — with the ExecStart line now pinned EXACTLY, which the golden never did."

data unprivileged_principal_witness_note: String = "Discriminating RED for the run-29822498755 regression class: the ci-runner principal (fleet_posix_accounts FleetAccountCiRunner) holds NO rsync/chown/rmdir grant and no write on the service-user-owned tree, so a bare rsync/chown/rmdir in either script is a deploy that fails on the host again. Working-byte rsync and repository convergence must instead ride the service-user oneshot unit (principal User=briansrls), and every mutation outside it must be one of the roster-granted sudo -n commands (fleet_posix_ci_runner_sudo_grants). Post-hoc admission of each sudo -n command against the ci_deploy_access grant envelope is the named residue (carried by the annotation on gunbc.live_deploy.emit install_d_owned_command)."

data belt_spawn_root_witness_note: String = "THE CLAIM THE BELT-TIMER MEMBER MOST NEEDED AND DID NOT HAVE (review 46541). Every other member's twin-safety follows from its PATH differing, which spec_owned_paths and the disjointness claim above already cover. The belt timer is the one member whose damage is not expressible as a path collision: both instances install their own unit at their own path, and the twin's unit can still drive PRODUCTION's tree, because what selects the tree is an argument inside the unit body rather than the unit's name. A path-level witness cannot see it, which is exactly the shape deployment_service_handler_note records for the serve handler.\\n\\nSo this reads the emitted body. The twin's belt unit must carry the twin's own spawn root, and must not carry production's — and because GUNBC_BELT_SPAWN_WORKDIR is fail-closed in belt_run_once_cli, a unit that carried neither would refuse at run time rather than silently default, which is the third state this pins shut.\\n\\nIt is discriminating in the direction that matters: deleting the Environment= line, or hardcoding either root in the emitter, reds it. The earlier conditional-membership shape would also have redded it, since the twin would have had no belt unit at all to carry a root."

data unobserved_client_refuses_before_emission_note: String = "THE VERSION WALL, AND THE REASON IT SITS AT EMISSION RATHER THAN IN THE SCRIPT. Scoped `serve <flags> off` arrived in tailscale client 1.52, so it is a fact about the binary installed on a host, not about tailscale. srv1 is measured at 1.102.2 and its target row records the measurement; no other fleet host has been measured, and asserting the capability for them from srv1 would be the same uncited generalization this whole change is repairing.\\n\\nAn in-script guard would have been the weaker answer: it puts a stop-the-line arm back among the teardowns, which is precisely the shape that once aborted every retract before it removed anything, and it only fires after the operator has already run the script. Refusing to EMIT means the dangerous artifact does not exist.\\n\\nThe claim needs all three arms because the failure mode is a two-into-one collapse. Unobserved and unsupported are DIFFERENT states — one host was never looked at, the other was looked at and cannot do it — and the tempting simplification is to treat unobserved as either capable (fail-open, the original defect) or as unsupported (which would silently misreport a host nobody has measured). Asserting that both refuse, that their refusals differ, and that the measured host still emits a real retract is what pins all three apart."
binding_declaration_evidence: data attempt_state_mode_derivation_witness_note: String = "This asserts the DERIVED mode, not a chosen one. srv1_attempt_state_directory declares exactly one dependent — the service principal, needing read, write, and execute — so managed_directory_permissions computes owner rwx and nothing for group or other, which serializes 0700. The witness compares against managed_directory_mode_octal rather than the literal `0700` on purpose: pinning the string would let the derivation break while the test stayed green by agreeing with itself in the wrong place, and it would also red for the RIGHT reason (a genuine new dependent widening the mode) as if it were a regression. What is actually being witnessed is that the emitted argv carries whatever the dependents imply — so this stays green when a dependent is legitimately added, and reds when emission stops consuming the derivation at all."

data twin_on_one_host_witness_note: String = "THE CLAIM THAT WAS UNWRITABLE BEFORE THIS CHANGE, and it is the whole point of it. deployment_owned_steps and deployment_service_config took no arguments, so there was exactly one deployment in the model and a second one on the SAME machine could not be constructed at all — not merely inconvenient, unexpressible. That is what proved host was the wrong axis: if the only thing that varies is which host, then two deployments on one host is a contradiction, and a model that makes it a contradiction has fused two independent facts.\\n\\nSo the test is the twin. Same target — one machine, one ssh host, one package manager — and a different instance, and every owned path, the unit, the tailscale mapping and the port must come out disjoint. srv1_lab is a real declared instance rather than a synthetic one, so this also states that the two dashboards already declared today CAN both be deployed, which was false an hour ago.\\n\\nThe conjunct that would survive a bad fix is the target equality. Without it the claim passes trivially if someone makes the twin differ by host, which is precisely the abstraction this replaces."

data teardown_safety_witness_note: String = "THE CLAIM THAT NAMES WHAT THE COLLISION WOULD HAVE COST, rather than only that paths differ. Every owned artifact is torn down by retract, so an overlap between two specs' owned sets is not an untidy duplicate — it is one deployment's retract deleting another's live files. The first version of the twin claim above went RED on exactly one path, the serve binary, because both instances read it from the host layout; a lab retract would have removed the binary production was executing.\\n\\nThis states the property directly in retract's own terms: nothing production owns appears in what the twin's teardown would remove. It is written over the retract order specifically, not the apply order, because teardown is the destructive direction and a claim about apply would not have caught it."

data emitted_effect_twin_note: String = "THE PATH-LIST TWIN CLAIM WAS COVERAGE BY ILLUSION AND THIS IS ITS REPLACEMENT. The previous claim compared five declared artifact paths and pinned count == 5, so its proof was bounded by the symbolic footprint — and three destructive effects lived outside it: the systemd unit hardcoded --function roadmap_serve_handle so a twin would IDENTIFY as production, tree-sync installed and deleted one host-wide unit and env file, and teardown ran a node-global `tailscale serve reset`. Every one of those passes a declared-member comparison while the emitted script is unsafe (review, 2026-07-30).\\n\\nSo this reads the EMITTED TEXT rather than the declared member list. It asserts over what apply and retract actually emit that production's identifying strings — its handler, its unit, its tree-sync files — appear in production's emission and are ABSENT from the twin's, and that the twin's own names are absent from production's. A string a reviewer can see in the emitted output is exactly the grain the previous claim could not reach.\\n\\nTHE APPLY HALF READS THE STEP PROJECTION, NOT THE ASSEMBLED PROGRAM (2026-09-14). test.claim.live_deploy.apply_emission_projection apply_emitted_steps_text is compose_host_script_mutate_steps over apply_intent_fragments — the mutate half apply_intent_from_effects hands to compose_host_script — with ONE input mocked: the membership effects, which in production come from observing the host and here are an empty host. So the dispatch is production's compose drop, and the strings asserted below are the bytes production's own producers emit when every Decide proceeds. Decide-only frame comments are outside this text. The reason is a cost ceiling rather than a modeling one, and it is stated at that module's header: one render of the assembled apply is ~194,000 eval steps against a per-claim ceiling of 72,300. The retract half still reads the assembled script, because retract has no such projection and no claim here needed one.\\n\\nThe negative direction is the load-bearing half. Asserting the twin contains its own names would pass even if it ALSO contained production's; only absence proves it cannot touch them. The tailscale conjunct asserts the refusal marker rather than a scoped command, because the CLI offers no per-port removal and the honest emission is a refusal — a claim expecting a scoped teardown would demand a widen that cannot be written safely."

data belt_spawn_root_witness_note: String = "THE CLAIM THE BELT-TIMER MEMBER MOST NEEDED AND DID NOT HAVE (review 46541). Every other member's twin-safety follows from its PATH differing, which spec_owned_paths and the disjointness claim above already cover. The belt timer is the one member whose damage is not expressible as a path collision: both instances install their own unit at their own path, and the twin's unit can still drive PRODUCTION's tree, because what selects the tree is an argument inside the unit body rather than the unit's name. A path-level witness cannot see it, which is exactly the shape deployment_service_handler_note records for the serve handler.\\n\\nSo this reads the emitted body. The twin's belt unit must carry the twin's own spawn root, and must not carry production's — and because GUNBC_BELT_SPAWN_WORKDIR is fail-closed in belt_run_once_cli, a unit that carried neither would refuse at run time rather than silently default, which is the third state this pins shut.\\n\\nIt is discriminating in the direction that matters: deleting the Environment= line, or hardcoding either root in the emitter, reds it. The earlier conditional-membership shape would also have redded it, since the twin would have had no belt unit at all to carry a root."

data twin_creates_its_own_bin_dir_note: String = "THE PARENT DIRECTORY WAS THE LAST srv1 LITERAL IN THE APPLY (review 45197). serve_binary became instance-derived while the step that creates its containing directory kept production's `/opt/gunbc/bin`, and `install` does not create missing parents — so a twin apply would reach the copy with nowhere to copy to and fail on what reads as a permissions problem.\\n\\nThe claim is stated in BOTH directions because only the negative half proves it. Asserting the twin creates its own bin directory passes even if the emission ALSO still creates production's; asserting production's literal is absent from the twin script is what closes it. The production conjunct pins that the derivation did not move production — /opt/gunbc/bin/gunbc has parent /opt/gunbc/bin, so its emitted command is unchanged, which the committed golden independently confirms."

data endpoint_identity_is_the_collision_axis_note: String = "THE CLAIM THE TWIN PROOF WAS MISSING, and its absence is why a green twin suite shipped a production-destroying apply. Every earlier twin claim in this file compares roots, ports, units, handlers and tree-sync files, and all of them passed while BOTH deployments configured the identical tailscale endpoint - because tailscale_serve_path was an invented label the emitter never read, and the emitted command derived from the port alone, which a bare `serve` ignores in favour of the default listener at the root mount.\\n\\nSo this asserts over the axis tailscale actually keys on, in BOTH directions and on BOTH scripts. The positive half - the twin carries its own --set-path - would pass against an emission that also bound production's endpoint, which is exactly the broken state. Only the negative half closes it: production's endpoint spelling must be ABSENT from the twin's apply and from the twin's retract, so the twin can neither steal the route nor remove it.\\n\\nThe retract conjuncts are not a restatement of the apply ones. The upstream requires every original flag on an off command, so apply and off can drift independently - an off missing --set-path targets the ROOT mount, which is production's, and would remove production's routing while exiting zero. Asserting the exact off spelling on each side is what ties the two directions to one endpoint value.\\n\\nONE CLAIM BECAME FOUR, ONE PER EMITTED SCRIPT, AND NOTHING WAS DROPPED (2026-08-23). The seven conjuncts below are the seven that were here; only their grouping changed. The regrouping is lossless because NO CONJUNCT EVER COMPARED TWO EMITTED SCRIPTS: disjointness is asserted by pattern negation against a command spelling derived from the OTHER spec, which is a cheap argv join, never that spec's emitted script. A reader who assumes a disjointness claim needs both scripts by construction will re-fuse these and re-cross the line - this row said exactly that in a PR body and it was wrong, caught by two independent readers of the conjuncts.\\n\\nWHY THE GROUPING MATTERED AT ALL, stated so this is not mistaken for tidiness: emitting a script costs about 6,714 interpreter node-evals per emitted shell WORD, so a claim's cost is the number of SCRIPTS it builds. Four scripts in one claim put this row at ~5009ms against the 5000ms CPU safety deadline then standing and it was INTERRUPTED BEFORE VERDICT - not passing, not failing, unknown - which is a strictly worse outcome than either verdict. One script per claim puts each row where the module's ordinary rows already sit, and a red now locates which script and which direction rather than which of seven conjuncts.\\n\\nTHIS IS A LOCAL UNBLOCK AND NOT THE REPAIR, AND CONFLATING THEM IS THE REAL RISK HERE. Sixteen rows in this module sit at 70-96% of the same limit; this regrouping moves the one row that crossed and leaves the population where it was. The cost is systemic - every emit consumer in the corpus pays the same per-word rate - and its measurement, its falsified hypotheses and its next-rung trigger are docs/probes/live_deploy_emit_witness_cost_attribution_2026-08-23.md. The next fleet runner-slot width increase lengthens the emitted script again and the next-highest row crosses.\\n\\nONE THING THIS REGROUPING MAKES HARDER, DECLARED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. The claim as written is LITERAL: it negates a spelling. The strictly stronger form is RELATIONAL - assert the two emitted endpoint values differ FROM EACH OTHER, which catches a drift that keeps both spellings absent from each other's script while still colliding. That form genuinely needs both scripts in one claim, so adopting it re-fuses two of these rows and re-crosses the line at today's per-word cost. It is therefore gated on the emit-cost lane rather than on anyone's appetite, and it is named here so the stronger claim is a known deferral and not an idea nobody had."

data why_the_crate_is_this_small_doc: String = "The crate is one no-dependency bin because the witness cost derives from what it proves (DESIGN witness-cost ruling): the subject is the round trip from a real cargo invocation to a real digest, and the smallest crate that crosses that boundary is the requirement plus one. A larger or realistic-looking crate would buy verisimilitude and nothing else, and a dependency would make the witness need a registry it has no reason to reach. Each claim builds its OWN crate in its OWN mktemp directory and nothing is shared between them, which is why the cost is stated as three builds of a no-dependency hello-world rather than one. This file therefore does NOT witness the one-build-one-artifact control the lane owes: that control is about reusing a built artifact across invocations, and asserting it here — where every claim deliberately starts from an empty target directory — would be naming a property nothing in this file exercises."

data mktemp_path_is_untrimmed_note: String = "shell.Mktemp.Dir models path as FilePath taken straight from stdout, and mktemp prints a trailing newline, so the value carries it. Interpolating it into a longer path therefore puts a newline INSIDE the path and every subsequent write refuses — which is how this witness first failed, at the fixture write rather than anywhere near the subject. Trimming here is a call-site repair, not the fix: the modeling gap is that the operation projects a line of stdout to FilePath without saying the projection strips the terminator. It is left alone deliberately because the same field is consumed raw at other call sites whose transports tolerate it, so changing the shared operation is a separate change with its own blast radius, not a rider on this one."

data digest_identity_claim_is_permanent_note: String = "the_digest_is_of_the_file_cargo_named_not_of_some_other_real_file DOES NOT RETIRE, and this note exists because it will one day look redundant. Today it is the only claim in this file that fails when the producer digests the WRONG REAL FILE: materialization, the carried path, and the refusal arms all stay green under that mutation, because none of them is a function of which file was read. ObservedArtifactDigest is sole_constructor over a validated digest and carries no referent, so wrong-file is writable at the mint and invisible to every consumer downstream of it — forgery-from-text is closed, forgery-from-a-different-real-file is not. RUNG, HONESTLY: mechanically preventable, and this claim IS the mechanism — not a backstop to a construction wall, because no such wall exists here. Three were proposed and all three were measured and abandoned, which is why the rung is stated rather than promised. Sealing the mint to an observation binding digest to subject would make 39 hermetic claims unconstructible across two lanes; sealing this producer's input is worse, because Sha512FileObservation is an extdeps type with 35 construction sites and two production consumers (gunbc.package_delivery, gunbc.provider_wire_evidence) that have no stake in this lane and would pay for a guarantee they did not ask for; and a narrower sealed observation closes the production hole only to require an admitted test-construction path, which is the escape hatch DESIGN §5 forbids wearing a better name. The circle is not an accident of these carriers: wrong-file is unforgeable only if an observation cannot be hand-authored, and every hermetic arm exists BECAUSE it can be. NEXT-RUNG TRIGGER, and it is the repository's already-tracked one rather than a coined local one: DESIGN §4b unforgeable construction for carrier-borne invariants, whose candidate wall sole_constructor is recorded as UNVERIFIED for generic refinement carriers and construction forms. This lane is downstream of that wall, not a reason for it. If it lands, this claim becomes the executed evidence that the higher rung stays real (§4b dissolution-on-climb: production machinery dissolves, discriminating evidence stays enrolled) — deleting it then would recreate specification-without-execution one rung up."
